title: # tests(mobile): E2E transaction-request flow for WalletConnect dApps
description:
## What it solves

Resolves: [WA-2326](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2326/e2e-transaction-request-flow)

## How this PR fixes it

Five Maestro flows for the WC tx-request path: happy (real signing + staging `/propose`, `safeTxHash` delivery asserted end-to-end), reject (5000), EIP-5792 batch (`{ id: safeTxHash }`), read-only Safe (4100, no sheet), CGW failure (500 via e2e fetch interceptor; rejected only on abandon — `-32603` is never sent by design).

E2E-only harness: the fake WalletKit records dApp responses, `WcResponseIndicator` exposes them as Maestro markers, and fixture values carry wei jitter so reruns can't collide on the same safeTxHash.

Includes the not-yet-merged WA-2325 commit (tx flows depend on its session seeding).

## How to test it

```bash
yarn workspace @safe-global/mobile e2e:metro-ios
# Simulator: Features → Face ID → Enrolled, then:
maestro test --include-tags walletconnect-dapps apps/mobile/e2e
```

## Affected flows

- None in production (e2e overrides only, plus one `testID` in `ReviewFooter`).

## Blast radius

- Shared e2e harness (pairing/management suites still pass); happy/batch runs append one queued tx per run to the Sepolia staging test Safe.

## Risks / not checked

- batch + cgw-failure flows not yet green on a simulator; iOS only.

## Visual summary

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[synth eth_sendTransaction] --> B[sheet → review → sign]
    B --> C[CGW /propose 200 or mocked 500]
    C --> D[respondSessionRequest recorded]
    D --> E[Maestro asserts hash-match marker]
```

## Checklist

- [x] I've tested the branch on mobile 📱
- [x] I've documented how it affects the analytics (if at all) 📊
- [x] I've written a unit/e2e test for it (if applicable) 🧑‍💻
- [x] I've listed affected flows and blast radius, and named what I did not verify 🎯

---

With the submission of this Pull Request, I confirm that I have read and agree to the terms of the [Contributor License Agreement](https://safe.global/cla).

findings.claim: The requestUrl handling supports string, URL, and Request inputs, but the tests only exercise the string case even though the app's CGW client, built on RTK's fetchBaseQuery, calls fetch with a Request object, meaning the branch the app actually uses (input.url) is untested; if that branch broke, unit tests would still pass and the only symptom would be an unexplained timeout in the tx-send-cgw-failure Maestro run.

The install-once, per-Metro-lifetime contract should be documented explicitly, or an uninstallProposeFetchMock() function should be exposed so tests running against the module in isolation can rebind.

None of the tests clear the pending request before calling respond, so they don't exercise the scenario the component's ref-based hash tracking was written for (the propose-success listener clearing the pending request in the same tick it sends the response). If the ref were replaced with a value computed from hashes during render, all six tests would still pass, meaning the tests would not catch a regression that would break the hash-match marker in the tx-send-happy.yml and tx-send-batch.yml flows.

The suite header still describes only a 'pairing & session-approval suite', but the suite now also includes connected-apps management flows and transaction-request flows, so the header should be updated to reflect all three groups.

extendedWaitUntil timeout values (e.g. 30000 for sign, 10000 for sheet) are duplicated across all five new Maestro flows, so a shared constants.yml or Maestro env variables would let a CI-slow timeout bump be made in one place instead of many.

The random wei amount added to each value causes every run of tx-send-happy and tx-send-batch to add new transactions to the queue of a Safe on staging that is shared with other test suites (assets and onboarding), and nothing ever clears these transactions out of the queue.

The final assertVisible check for text 'Send' in the pending list can pass because of a leftover transaction from a previous run rather than the transaction created by the current run, so it does not actually prove that this run's transaction was queued.

Object.keys(outstanding) order is insertion order, so treating the last key as the newest is not guaranteed by object key semantics; a comment tying this invariant to the one-outstanding-tx-per-test flow contract would prevent future readers from assuming ordering is guaranteed.

installProposeFetchMock captures global.fetch at install time and never restores it; if Jest test isolation unhooks or swaps global.fetch between suites, a second installProposeFetchMock() call returns early due to the module-scoped installed flag, silently leaving the interceptor uninstalled from the new fetch.
The assertVisible selector text: '.*0\.001.*' can match multiple UI surfaces that render this fixture value, making the assertion insufficiently specific.
The same assertion (expect(request.params.chainId).toBe(`eip155:${…}`)) appears on both line 587 and line 590, apparently left over from an edit, and the duplicate line should be removed.

A commit replaced an accurate comment with one claiming the state is shallow-cloned and that in-place mutation of a nested value would corrupt initialState and break reset(), but the code actually performs a full deep copy on store creation and again on reset(), so initialState cannot be corrupted and reset() still works; this gives readers an incorrect mental model of the store and should be reverted or reworded to state only what is true.
The same chainId assertion is duplicated, appearing at both line 141 and line 144 within the same test.
A comment still refers to "the ticket's 'Add a signer' CTA" even though a prior commit removed ticket references, leaving a stale reference that no longer makes sense to readers.

The setup failure should be surfaced as a marker (e.g. e2e-wc-setup-failed) via walletKitE2eState so flows can assertNotVisible it before proceeding, mirroring the existing rejectSessionCalled/lastRequestResponse side-channels.

The wei jitter formula combines Date.now() with an incrementing counter to avoid collisions, but two flows starting within the same wall-clock millisecond and hitting the same jitterSeq value across module reloads could theoretically still collide.

The doc comment states that state is shallow-cloned and that mutating a nested value would corrupt initialState and break reset(), but the code performs a deep clone of initialState both at creation and inside reset() (lines 30 and 50), so initialState cannot actually be corrupted this way. The comment therefore misrepresents the store's contract to future readers.

A commit removed ticket references from e2e comments, but this file still contains a comment referencing the ticket's 'Add a signer' CTA not existing in the implementation, which should be deleted or reworded to remove the ticket mention.

A raw private key is committed to the repository; even though it is a throwaway Sepolia-only key, committing raw keys attracts secret-scanner attention and creates false positives on downstream forks, so it should be gated behind an env var or documented as intentionally public.

chainId is hardcoded as '0xaa36a7' instead of being derived from mockedActiveAccount.chainId the way CAIP2 is built on line 28, so changing the fixture chain would silently break the batch flow without updating this value.

E2E_TX_OWNER_ADDRESS duplicates the first owner address from mockData.ts instead of referencing it, and a recipient address (0x81BdB0…) is repeated as a raw string at two other locations rather than a named constant, so if the fixture Safe's owners change these copies will silently drift and break the tx flows without an obvious cause.
The 1x1 red marker style is duplicated from the equivalent style already defined in TestCtrls.e2e.tsx:389 instead of being shared, creating redundant code that must be kept in sync manually.

setupWcDappsTx's promise rejection is only logged with console.error, which Maestro cannot observe; if storePrivateKey fails on a simulator due to biometrics/keychain issues, the flow proceeds to synthTxRequest and later fails with a confusing symptom that has no direct pointer back to the setup failure.

The useEffect has no dependency array, so it runs on every render since hashes = Object.keys(outstanding) produces a fresh array each render; it should depend on outstanding, or the ref update should be computed via useMemo on outstanding instead.
A private key is hardcoded in this setup file, which the root AGENTS.md rules forbid.

The assertVisible selector text: 'Send' matches any UI element containing the word 'Send' (action, button, or tab), so it should use a stable testID on the queued tx row or a more tightly scoped text match.
